name: Switch List
statusNote: A content source superseded at parity by Clear Board — its seven engine modules were absorbed byte-for-byte into Clear Board's Yard station — but kept live on its own page.
oneLiner: A free browser switching simulator for yard work — line switches, call PULL/SPOT/KICK moves, secure cuts, and build trains, with every mechanic tied to a real rule citation.
stack: Vanilla JavaScript (ES modules), no build step, no framework
Canvas 2D rendering, Web Audio synthesized sfx
Node used only for the offline solver/verification harness

components.name: geometry.js
components.desc: The schematic ladder-yard layout, switch positions, and car-type table.

components.name: model.js
components.desc: The rules brain — move mutators paired with pure validators, plus win-check and grading.

components.name: render.js + anim.js
components.desc: A pure draw function and a sequential tween driver.

components.name: puzzles.js
components.desc: 19 hand-authored puzzles with solver-baked par and optimal lines.

components.name: solver.js
components.desc: A Dijkstra solver over game states that imports the exact same model the UI uses.

components.name: tools/solve.mjs
components.desc: The Node CI harness — fails the build if any puzzle's par is wrong or suboptimal.

dataFlow: Clicking a switch toggles its lined state and repaints.
A chosen move runs a precheck first — illegal or fouling moves are refused immediately with a cited reason and never animate.
Legal moves animate, committing the state mutation partway through the tween.
A win check fires on the goal condition; grading compares moves to par, with joints as a secondary stat.
The solver replays every puzzle's candidate line through a fresh state to confirm it wins in exactly par moves.
integrations: Rules source of truth is CN Conductor Trainer's rulebook material and a citation index — switch-list never invents rule content
Absorbed byte-for-byte into clear-board's Yard station, where rule citations map to the shared mastery model
decisions: The headline scoring correction: the prototype optimized fewest joints and produced perverse lines, so moves became the primary par metric with joints a tiebreaker.
The solver never reimplements the rules — it imports the exact functions the UI calls, so solver/game divergence is structurally impossible.
Exactly one rule is introduced per difficulty tier.
Rulebook rules and Special Instructions carry visually distinct badges.
Fixed, authored puzzles over runtime generation — random generation was tried and abandoned.
Some puzzles carry a deliberately wrong manifest, to train checking the list against the yard.
